title: What does the last single digit tell us about nine?
description: Adding the digits of a number again and again until one digit is left gives its digital root, and that digit is the remainder on division by nine. Two numbers show the idea, one with remainder two and one that is a multiple of nine. Keeko's doubt is that the digital root of four thousand five hundred eighty one is eighteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep adding the digits until one digit is left, and that digit is the remainder on division by nine, with nine meaning no remainder. Watch for students who stop at a two digit sum such as eighteen.

source: Find the digital roots of 489710 and 4581, and say what they tell you about division by 9
video_script.why: A learner finds a digital root by adding digits until one digit is left, and reads it as the remainder on division by nine.
video_script.anchor: the numbers 489710 and 4581 with their digits written out
video_script.wrong_answer: the digital root of four thousand five hundred eighty one is eighteen
video_script.wrong_move: adds the digits once and stops at the two digit sum
video_script.payoff_line: The digital roots are two and nine.

final_answer.value: 489710 has digital root 2 (remainder 2); 4581 has digital root 9 (a multiple of 9)
final_answer.spoken: the digital root of four lakh eighty nine thousand seven hundred ten is two with remainder two, and the digital root of four thousand five hundred eighty one is nine, a multiple of nine

hold_back: 489710 has digital root 2 (remainder 2); 4581 has digital root 9 (a multiple of 9)
maths_rules: 29 = 3 × 9 + 2, so 489710 leaves remainder 2 on division by 9
a digital root has a single digit, so 18 is not a digital root
video_script.design: One idea: repeat the digit sum until one digit is left, and read it as the remainder on division by nine. Assumes the digit sum test for nine. The two numbers stay on the board all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about two numbers. The first is four lakh eighty nine thousand seven hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is four thousand five hundred eighty one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We add the digits of each number again and again, until one digit is left.
What does that last digit tell us about dividing by nine?

beats.on_screen: the two numbers stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number, then its digit sum, then the digit sum of that sum, with an arrow stopping at one digit labelled digital root

marks.add: an arrow from a number to its digit sum appears
marks.again: a second arrow adds the digits of the sum
marks.name: the single digit at the end is labelled digital root

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Add the digits of a number. If the sum has two digits, add those digits again.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Keep going until only one digit is left.
<bookmark mark='name'/>That single digit is called the digital root of the number.

marks.given: the two numbers are written with their digits apart

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers four lakh eighty nine thousand seven hundred ten, and four thousand five hundred eighty one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the digital root of each number, and what it tells about division by 9

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the digital root of each number. Then we see what it says about nine.

marks.root: 1 + 1 = 2 is written and 2 is boxed as the digital root

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, take four lakh eighty nine thousand seven hundred ten. Four plus eight plus nine plus seven plus one plus zero is twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Twenty nine has two digits, so we add again. Two plus nine is eleven.
<bookmark mark='root'/>Eleven has two digits too. One plus one is two, so the digital root is two.

beats.on_screen: 29 = 3 × 9 + 2, so 489710 leaves remainder 2 on division by 9

marks.rem: remainder 2 is written beside the digital root 2

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, the digit sum leaves the same remainder as the number on division by nine. Twenty nine is three nines and two more.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>The number leaves remainder two on division by nine, the same as its digital root.

marks.root: 1 + 8 = 9 is written and 9 is boxed as the digital root

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, take four thousand five hundred eighty one. Four plus five plus eight plus one is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='root'/>Eighteen has two digits, so we add again. One plus eight is nine, and the digital root is nine.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>A root of nine means nothing is left over. Nine times five hundred nine makes four thousand five hundred eighty one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 489710 has digital root 2 (remainder 2); 4581 has digital root 9 (a multiple of 9)

marks.ans: the two digital roots are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The digital roots are two and nine. The first number leaves remainder two on division by nine, and the second is a multiple of nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number 4581
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 4 + 5 + 8 + 1 = 18, digital root 18; the digits 1 and 8 of 18 light up; the bubble is struck through

marks.two: the digits 1 and 8 of 18 light up
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 1 + 8 = 9 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the digital root of four thousand five hundred eighty one is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='two'/>But eighteen still has two digits, and a digital root has only one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Keeko stopped one step too soon. One plus eight is nine.
